title: Large nonempty Fourier coefficient
statement: There is a constant $C>0$ such that for every natural number $n$ and every function $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ taking values in $\{-1,1\}$ and having variance at least $1/2$ under the uniform measure, there is a nonempty set $S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ such that $|S|\le C I(f)$ and $\exp(-C I(f)^2)\le\widehat f(S)^2$. Here $I(f)$ is the total influence and $\widehat f(S)$ is the uniform Fourier–Walsh coefficient at $S$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a real-valued function on the Boolean cube
the variance of $f$ is at least $1/2$ under the uniform measure
replaced: There exists an absolute $C>0$ such that for every $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ under the uniform law with $\operatorname{Var}(f)\ge1/2$, there is a nonempty $S\subseteq[n]$ with $|S|\le CI(f)$ and $\widehat f(S)^2\ge\exp(-CI(f)^2)$. For a real cube function $h$, define $I_i(h)=\tfrac14\mathbb E_x(h(x)-h(x^{(i)}))^2$, where $x^{(i)}$ flips coordinate $i$ and $\mathbb E_x$ is uniform expectation, and $I(h)=\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}I_i(h)$.
